_comment: Generic marker catalog: English display name, body-system group, plain-language meaning and aliases (English, German, a few Hindi). Report values are matched by name or alias (case-insensitive). unit: the preferred display unit. units: other accepted units, where value in unit = value x factor, each with its source (src). plausible: [min, max] in the preferred unit, sanity bounds that catch reading errors such as a lost decimal point; they are NOT medical reference ranges. alt: the paired marker for the same test in other units (share vs count, HbA1c % vs mmol/mol); the unit on a report decides between them. Add your lab's own names (any language) as aliases in private/markers.json, which is merged over this file.

markers.name: Blood pressure: top number (left)
markers.meaning: The pressure in your arteries when your heart squeezes. A single reading cannot diagnose high blood pressure.

markers.name: Blood pressure: bottom number (left)
markers.meaning: The pressure in your arteries between heartbeats. It is read together with the top number.

markers.name: Blood pressure: top number (right)
markers.meaning: The pressure in your arteries when your heart squeezes. A single reading cannot diagnose high blood pressure.

markers.name: Blood pressure: bottom number (right)
markers.meaning: The pressure in your arteries between heartbeats. It is read together with the top number.

markers.name: Pulse pressure (left)
markers.meaning: The difference between the top and bottom blood-pressure numbers. It is not your heart rate.

markers.name: Pulse pressure (right)
markers.meaning: The difference between the top and bottom blood-pressure numbers. It is not your heart rate.

markers.name: Average artery pressure
markers.meaning: An estimate of the average pressure driving blood through your arteries during a heartbeat.

markers.name: Ankle-to-arm pressure ratio
markers.meaning: Compares blood pressure at your ankle with your arm to screen circulation in the legs.

markers.name: Resting heart rate
markers.meaning: How many times your heart beats each minute while resting. Stress, illness and activity affect it.

markers.name: Pulse wave speed
markers.meaning: How quickly a pressure wave moves along an artery. It is a screening estimate related to artery stiffness; device and age matter.

markers.name: Screening blood sugar
markers.meaning: Sugar in your blood at a screening check-up where fasting status may be unknown. It is kept separate from fasting laboratory results.

markers.name: Triglycerides
markers.meaning: A type of fat carried in the blood. Meals and fasting status can affect the result.

units.src: triglycerides are reported as triolein, molar mass 885.4 g/mol: 1 mmol/L = 88.54 mg/dL. https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/5497163

markers.name: Total cholesterol
markers.meaning: The total cholesterol carried by different particles in your blood. LDL and HDL help explain this total.

units.src: cholesterol molar mass 386.65 g/mol: 1 mmol/L = 38.665 mg/dL. https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/5997

markers.name: LDL cholesterol
markers.meaning: Cholesterol in particles that can build up in artery walls. Your ideal level depends on overall cardiovascular risk.

units.src: cholesterol molar mass 386.65 g/mol: 1 mmol/L = 38.665 mg/dL. https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/5997

markers.name: HDL cholesterol
markers.meaning: Cholesterol in particles involved in moving cholesterol back to the liver. It is one part of the heart-risk picture.

units.src: cholesterol molar mass 386.65 g/mol: 1 mmol/L = 38.665 mg/dL. https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/5997

markers.name: ALT: liver-related enzyme
markers.meaning: An enzyme mainly found in liver cells. A raised result can indicate irritation or injury, but does not tell you the cause.

units.src: SI enzyme units: 1 U = 1 µmol/min and 1 kat = 1 mol/s, so 1 µkat/L = 60 U/L.

markers.name: AST: liver and muscle enzyme
markers.meaning: An enzyme found in the liver and muscles. It helps interpret other enzyme results, rather than diagnosing a cause alone.

units.src: SI enzyme units: 1 U = 1 µmol/min and 1 kat = 1 mol/s, so 1 µkat/L = 60 U/L.

markers.name: GGT: liver and bile-duct enzyme
markers.meaning: An enzyme that helps assess the liver and bile ducts. Medicines and alcohol can also affect it.

units.src: SI enzyme units: 1 U = 1 µmol/min and 1 kat = 1 mol/s, so 1 µkat/L = 60 U/L.

markers.name: Blood oxygen level
markers.meaning: An estimate of the percentage of hemoglobin carrying oxygen, measured by a sensor.

markers.name: Air blown out: % of expected (FVC)
markers.meaning: The total air you can forcefully blow out, compared with an expected value for someone of your size and age. This alone cannot diagnose lung disease.

markers.name: Air blown out: volume (FVC)
markers.meaning: Liters of air you forcefully blow out after a deep breath. This is not your total lung capacity.

markers.name: First-second breathing: % of expected (FEV1)
markers.meaning: How much air you blow out in the first second, compared with an expected value. Effort and technique matter.

markers.name: First-second breathing: volume (FEV1)
markers.meaning: Liters of air blown out in the first second of a forced breath.

markers.name: First-second share of breath (FEV1/FVC)
markers.meaning: The percentage of a full forced breath that comes out in the first second. It helps assess airflow narrowing.

markers.name: Peak airflow: % of expected
markers.meaning: Your fastest breathing-out speed compared with an expected value. It is especially sensitive to effort.

markers.name: Peak airflow: speed
markers.meaning: The fastest speed of air during a forceful breath out, in liters per second.

markers.name: Mid-breath airflow: % of expected
markers.meaning: Average airflow through the middle of a forced breath. It varies with technique and is not diagnostic on its own.

markers.name: Weight
markers.meaning: Your body weight on the day it was measured. Older measurements do not show your current weight.

markers.name: Body mass index (BMI)
markers.meaning: Weight relative to height. It is a broad screening measure and does not distinguish muscle from fat.

markers.name: Estimated resting energy use
markers.meaning: A device estimate of energy used at rest each day. It is not a recommended daily food allowance.

markers.name: Estimated body water
markers.meaning: The device-estimated proportion of your weight that is water. Hydration affects this estimate.

markers.name: Estimated bone mineral mass
markers.meaning: A body-composition device estimate of bone minerals. It is not a bone-density scan or an osteoporosis test.

markers.name: Estimated body fat: weight
markers.meaning: The estimated total weight of body fat. This is a device estimate, not a direct measurement.

markers.name: Estimated body fat: percentage
markers.meaning: The estimated share of your body weight that is fat. Device and hydration differences affect comparisons.

markers.name: Internal abdominal fat rating
markers.meaning: A device-specific rating of fat around abdominal organs. It is a score, not kilograms or a percentage.

markers.name: Reported fat-free mass
markers.meaning: The report’s estimate of non-fat tissue. Devices define this differently, so compare only results from the same method.

markers.name: Estimated body fat: trunk
markers.meaning: The device-estimated fat percentage in your trunk. It is useful only with the method and other body-composition results in mind.

markers.name: Reported lean mass: trunk
markers.meaning: The report’s estimated non-fat tissue in your trunk. Regional values are device-dependent and may not add up to a whole-body total.

markers.name: Estimated body fat: arms
markers.meaning: The device-estimated fat percentage in your arms. It is useful only with the method and other body-composition results in mind.

markers.name: Reported lean mass: arms
markers.meaning: The report’s estimated non-fat tissue in your arms. Regional values are device-dependent and may not add up to a whole-body total.

markers.name: Estimated body fat: legs
markers.meaning: The device-estimated fat percentage in your legs. It is useful only with the method and other body-composition results in mind.

markers.name: Reported lean mass: legs
markers.meaning: The report’s estimated non-fat tissue in your legs. Regional values are device-dependent and may not add up to a whole-body total.

markers.name: Hemoglobin: oxygen-carrying protein
markers.meaning: The protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen. A low result means anemia; other tests help explain why.

units.src: SI prefixes: 1 g/L = 0.1 g/dL (1 dL = 0.1 L).
hemoglobin per heme subunit, molar mass 16,114 g/mol (the SI convention behind mmol/L reports): 1 mmol/L = 1.6114 g/dL. ICSH/IFCC, Clin Chim Acta 1979;96:183-8 (doi:10.1016/0009-8981(79)90071-0).

markers.name: Red blood cell size (MCV)
markers.meaning: The average size of your red blood cells. Smaller or larger cells can point to different causes and are read with the rest of the blood count.

markers.name: Red blood cell count
markers.meaning: The number of oxygen-carrying red blood cells. A high count does not necessarily mean hemoglobin is adequate.

markers.name: Hemoglobin per red cell (MCH)
markers.meaning: The average amount of oxygen-carrying protein inside each red blood cell.

markers.name: Hemoglobin concentration in red cells
markers.meaning: How concentrated the oxygen-carrying protein is inside your red blood cells.

units.src: SI prefixes: 1 g/L = 0.1 g/dL (1 dL = 0.1 L).
hemoglobin per heme subunit, molar mass 16,114 g/mol (the SI convention behind mmol/L reports): 1 mmol/L = 1.6114 g/dL. ICSH/IFCC, Clin Chim Acta 1979;96:183-8 (doi:10.1016/0009-8981(79)90071-0).

markers.name: Blood volume occupied by red cells
markers.meaning: The percentage of your blood volume made up of red blood cells.

units.src: a fraction of 1: 1 L/L = 100 %.

markers.name: White blood cell count
markers.meaning: The number of immune cells in your blood. A result in range does not exclude an infection.

units.src: SI prefixes: 1 µL = 10⁻⁶ L, so 1/µL = 0.001 × 10³/µL (= 10⁹/L).

markers.name: Platelet count
markers.meaning: Small blood components that help stop bleeding by forming clots.

units.src: SI prefixes: 1 µL = 10⁻⁶ L, so 1/µL = 0.001 × 10³/µL (= 10⁹/L).

markers.name: Variation in red blood cell size
markers.meaning: How much your red cells differ in size. A raised result means there is a wider mix of sizes.

markers.name: Red cells with low hemoglobin concentration
markers.meaning: The percentage of red cells with a low concentration of hemoglobin.

markers.name: Red cells with high hemoglobin concentration
markers.meaning: The percentage of red cells with a high concentration of hemoglobin; interpreted alongside the full blood count.

markers.name: CRP: inflammation marker
markers.meaning: A protein that rises with inflammation. It does not identify the cause or the location on its own.

units.src: SI prefixes: 1 mg/dL = 10 mg/L (1 dL = 0.1 L).

markers.name: Procalcitonin: infection-related marker
markers.meaning: A marker used in assessing some bacterial illnesses. A low result cannot rule out a localized infection.

markers.name: Creatinine: kidney blood marker
markers.meaning: A waste product from normal muscle activity. The kidneys filter it from the blood.

units.src: creatinine molar mass 113.12 g/mol: 1 mg/dL = 88.42 µmol/L. https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/588

markers.name: Estimated kidney filtering ability
markers.meaning: An estimate of kidney filtration based on blood creatinine. It is an estimate, not a percentage of kidney function.

markers.name: Urea: protein-breakdown waste
markers.meaning: Waste formed when your body processes protein. Kidney function, hydration and diet can influence it.

units.src: urea molar mass 60.06 g/mol: 1 mmol/L = 6.006 mg/dL. https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/1176

markers.name: Blood urea nitrogen (BUN)
markers.meaning: The nitrogen part of urea, a waste product the kidneys clear. It is a different number from urea (urea is about 2.14 times BUN), so the two are kept apart.

units.src: urea carries two nitrogen atoms (2 × 14.007 g/mol): 1 mmol/L urea = 2.801 mg/dL urea nitrogen. https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/1176

markers.name: Uric acid
markers.meaning: Waste from breaking down substances called purines. High levels can contribute to gout in some people.

units.src: uric acid molar mass 168.11 g/mol: 1 mg/dL = 59.48 µmol/L. https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/1175

markers.name: Iron circulating in blood
markers.meaning: Iron available in the bloodstream at that moment. It does not measure iron stores.

units.src: iron atomic weight 55.845: 1 µmol/L = 5.585 µg/dL. https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/23925

markers.name: Ferritin: iron stores
markers.meaning: A protein that stores iron inside cells. The blood level is the usual marker of the body’s iron stores, though inflammation can raise it.

markers.name: Soluble transferrin receptor (sTfR)
markers.meaning: A protein that rises when cells need more iron. It is less affected by inflammation than ferritin and is read alongside it.

markers.name: Potassium
markers.meaning: An electrolyte that helps nerves, muscles and the heart work normally. The kidneys keep it in balance.

units.src: monovalent ions: 1 mEq/L = 1 mmol/L.

markers.name: Sodium
markers.meaning: An electrolyte that helps control fluid balance in the body. It reflects water balance as much as salt intake.

units.src: monovalent ions: 1 mEq/L = 1 mmol/L.

markers.name: Folate (vitamin B9)
markers.meaning: A vitamin needed to make DNA and healthy red blood cells. Diet and some medicines affect the level.

units.src: folic acid molar mass 441.4 g/mol: 1 ng/mL = 2.266 nmol/L. https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/135398658

markers.name: Iron transport protein
markers.meaning: A protein that carries iron through the bloodstream.

units.src: SI prefixes: 1 g/L = 100 mg/dL (1 dL = 0.1 L).

markers.name: Iron transport capacity in use
markers.meaning: The percentage of transferrin’s iron-carrying sites that are filled. It is interpreted with iron stores and inflammation.

markers.name: Fasting blood sugar
markers.meaning: Blood sugar measured after fasting. Kept separate from screening results whose fasting status is unclear.

units.src: glucose molar mass 180.16 g/mol: 1 mmol/L = 18.016 mg/dL. https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/5793

markers.name: Average blood sugar (HbA1c)
markers.meaning: Reflects blood sugar over roughly the previous two to three months. Some red-cell conditions affect its reliability.

markers.name: Average blood sugar: alternate units
markers.meaning: The same HbA1c test expressed in mmol/mol rather than percent. This is not a separate measurement.

markers.name: Total bilirubin
markers.meaning: A substance produced when red blood cells break down, then processed by the liver. A rise has several possible explanations.

units.src: bilirubin molar mass 584.66 g/mol: 1 mg/dL = 17.10 µmol/L. https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/5280352

markers.name: Processed bilirubin
markers.meaning: The part of bilirubin already processed by the liver. It helps interpret total bilirubin.

units.src: bilirubin molar mass 584.66 g/mol: 1 mg/dL = 17.10 µmol/L. https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/5280352

markers.name: ALP: bile-duct and bone enzyme
markers.meaning: An enzyme linked to the bile ducts and bones. Other tests help identify the source of a change.

units.src: SI enzyme units: 1 U = 1 µmol/min and 1 kat = 1 mol/s, so 1 µkat/L = 60 U/L.

markers.name: Lipase: digestive enzyme
markers.meaning: An enzyme involved in digesting fats, mainly made by the pancreas.

units.src: SI enzyme units: 1 U = 1 µmol/min and 1 kat = 1 mol/s, so 1 µkat/L = 60 U/L.

markers.name: Amylase: digestive enzyme
markers.meaning: An enzyme that helps digest starch, made by the pancreas and salivary glands.

units.src: SI enzyme units: 1 U = 1 µmol/min and 1 kat = 1 mol/s, so 1 µkat/L = 60 U/L.

markers.name: CK: muscle enzyme
markers.meaning: An enzyme released from muscles. Exercise, muscle injury and medicines can raise it.

units.src: SI enzyme units: 1 U = 1 µmol/min and 1 kat = 1 mol/s, so 1 µkat/L = 60 U/L.

markers.name: CK-MB: muscle enzyme subtype
markers.meaning: A subtype of CK used in some assessments of muscle or heart injury. It cannot establish or exclude a heart problem alone.

markers.name: LDH: general tissue enzyme
markers.meaning: An enzyme found in many tissues. Changes are nonspecific and require context.

units.src: SI enzyme units: 1 U = 1 µmol/min and 1 kat = 1 mol/s, so 1 µkat/L = 60 U/L.

markers.name: Non-HDL cholesterol
markers.meaning: Total cholesterol minus HDL. It captures cholesterol in several particles associated with artery risk.

units.src: cholesterol molar mass 386.65 g/mol: 1 mmol/L = 38.665 mg/dL. https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/5997

markers.name: Total blood protein
markers.meaning: The combined amount of albumin and globulins in your blood.

units.src: SI prefixes: 1 g/L = 0.1 g/dL (1 dL = 0.1 L).

markers.name: Albumin: main blood protein
markers.meaning: A protein made by the liver that carries substances and helps keep fluid in the bloodstream.

units.src: SI prefixes: 1 g/L = 0.1 g/dL (1 dL = 0.1 L).

markers.name: Albumin share of blood proteins
markers.meaning: Albumin expressed as a percentage of proteins in a protein-separation test.

markers.name: Calcium
markers.meaning: A mineral important for bones, nerves and muscles. Blood calcium is not a measure of bone density.

units.src: calcium atomic weight 40.078: 1 mmol/L = 4.008 mg/dL. https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/5460341
calcium is divalent: 1 mEq/L = 0.5 mmol/L = 2.004 mg/dL. https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/5460341

markers.name: Magnesium
markers.meaning: A mineral involved in muscle, nerve and many enzyme functions.

units.src: magnesium atomic weight 24.305: 1 mmol/L = 2.4305 mg/dL. https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/5462224
magnesium is divalent: 1 mEq/L = 0.5 mmol/L = 1.2153 mg/dL. https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/5462224

markers.name: Chloride
markers.meaning: An electrolyte involved in fluid and acid-base balance.

units.src: monovalent ions: 1 mEq/L = 1 mmol/L.

markers.name: Phosphate
markers.meaning: A mineral involved in bones and cellular energy.

units.src: phosphate is reported as phosphorus, atomic weight 30.974: 1 mmol/L = 3.097 mg/dL. https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/5462309

markers.name: Vitamin B12
markers.meaning: A vitamin needed for nerves and blood-cell production. Low levels can matter even when the blood count looks normal.

units.src: cobalamin (cyanocobalamin) molar mass 1355.4 g/mol: 1 pg/mL = 0.7378 pmol/L. https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/5311498

markers.name: Vitamin D
markers.meaning: The usual blood marker of vitamin D status, which helps regulate calcium and support bone health.

units.src: 25-hydroxyvitamin D3 (calcifediol) molar mass 400.6 g/mol: 1 ng/mL = 2.496 nmol/L. https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/5283731

markers.name: Active thyroid hormone (free T3)
markers.meaning: The freely available form of one thyroid hormone. It helps regulate metabolism.

units.src: triiodothyronine molar mass 650.97 g/mol: 1 pg/mL = 1.536 pmol/L. https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/5920

markers.name: Thyroid hormone supply (free T4)
markers.meaning: The freely available form of a hormone made by the thyroid. The body converts some of it to T3.

units.src: thyroxine molar mass 776.87 g/mol: 1 ng/dL = 12.87 pmol/L. https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/5819

markers.name: Thyroid control signal (TSH)
markers.meaning: The pituitary gland’s signal telling the thyroid how much hormone to make.
